ui.penguin.title: ECB penguin lab
ui.penguin.intro: Encrypt a picture with AES and look at the ciphertext as pixels. In ECB mode, equal 16-byte blocks give equal ciphertext blocks, so the shape survives encryption.
ui.penguin.key.label: Key (16 bytes as hex)
ui.penguin.iv.label: IV (16 bytes as hex)
ui.penguin.iv.fixedHint: Fixed here so the result is reproducible. Real CBC needs a fresh random IV for every message.
ui.penguin.upload.label: Use your own picture
ui.penguin.upload.hint: It is scaled down to at most {{max}} pixels per side. Your picture stays in your browser and is never uploaded.
ui.penguin.upload.failed: This file could not be read as an image.
ui.penguin.original.caption: Original
ui.penguin.original.altPenguin: Original image: a flat-colour cartoon penguin with a red scarf, standing on ice, {{width}} × {{height}} pixels.
ui.penguin.original.altUpload: Original image: your picture “{{name}}”, scaled to {{width}} × {{height}} pixels.
ui.penguin.encrypted.caption: Encrypted (AES-{{mode}})
ui.penguin.encrypted.alt: The ciphertext of the original image under AES-{{mode}}, drawn as pixels: {{repeated}} of {{total}} 16-byte ciphertext blocks repeat an earlier block.
ui.penguin.result.ecb: AES-ECB: {{repeated}} of {{total}} ciphertext blocks repeat an earlier block. Equal plaintext blocks give equal ciphertext blocks, so the outlines of flat areas show through.
ui.penguin.result.cbc: AES-CBC: {{repeated}} of {{total}} ciphertext blocks repeat an earlier block. Chaining makes every block depend on all blocks before it, so the picture turns into noise.
ui.penguin.padding: Only the colour bytes are encrypted (red, green, blue; no alpha). They are padded with PKCS#7 to whole 16-byte blocks; the padding is not drawn.
ui.penguin.error.keyLength: The key must be exactly 16 bytes (32 hex digits) long; this one has {{length}}.
ui.penguin.error.ivLength: The IV must be exactly 16 bytes (32 hex digits) long; this one has {{length}}.
